answer: Dynamic Resource Toll Routing charges every routing node an escalating fee based on local request density. As an agent spawns clones to flood the network, local traffic surges toward a localized congestion zenith, exponentially driving up the cost of message propagation. Attackers bleed capital maintaining active channels through this friction plume, because resource exhaustion outpaces utility. Honest agents scattered across a sparse topology avoid this congestion, finding a cost oasis where fees remain flat and operation stays viable.
